page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.2xlarge is an ARM-based compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 8 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.5 GHz based on the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture, with one execution thread per core and no simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. There is no bundled local storage, requiring persistent storage needs to be handled via Elastic Block Store (EBS) or network volumes. Baseline network throughput is rated at 12 Gbps, and no discrete graphics accelerators are provisioned.

Benchmark results highlight solid multi-threaded capability and network-adjacent performance. The instance achieves a stress-ng multi-core score of 12,130.94 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 5,435.0, reflecting efficient scaling across its dedicated physical cores. Application tests show 9.2 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.68 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, supported by an uncached read memory bandwidth of 119.78 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded processing reflects architectural limitations, with Geekbench single-core scoring at 946.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 20.35 GB/sec.

The 1:2 memory allocation and high baseline network bandwidth position the instance as a cost-efficient platform for distributed and parallel computational jobs. Its hardware balance favors multi-threaded compilation workflows (Geekbench Clang compile score of 8,571.0), containerized web servers, and high-throughput network proxy layers. Workloads reliant on single-thread instruction throughput, local NVMe storage speeds, or large memory capacities will encounter clear performance constraints on this profile.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gn.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the 64-bit ARM Neoverse-N1 Graviton processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features 8 dedicated physical cores with 8 vCPUs (single thread per core), 16.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core), 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and zero local storage, requiring network-attached storage. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the instance demonstrates balanced multi-core throughput, registering 12,130.94 in stress-ng multi-core tests, 9.2 million Redis SET operations per second, and 9.68 GB/s static web serving throughput. However, single-core benchmarks remain modest, reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 946.0 and low compression speeds. The 1:2 memory-to-compute ratio provides cost-effective dedicated compute capacity for parallelized microservices, Clang software compilation, network-bound web serving, and distributed caching, though it is less suited for memory-intensive datasets or tasks reliant on local NVMe storage.

16.0 GB system memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and 12 Gbps baseline network throughput
